title: The Company That Changed Its Mind
subtitle: In 2014 Microsoft was very rich, but it was falling behind. A new boss changed how people worked together — and the company grew bigger than ever.

vocab.def: The person who is in charge of other people at work.
vocab.ex: Satya Nadella became Microsoft's new boss in 2014.

vocab.def: How people in a group or company usually think and behave.
vocab.ex: The culture at Microsoft needed to change.

vocab.def: To try to win against other people or companies.
vocab.ex: Teams inside the company competed against each other.

vocab.def: To give part of something to other people, or use it together.
vocab.ex: The teams did not share ideas.

vocab.def: Something that is wrong, or a wrong decision.
vocab.ex: The new boss said he made a mistake.

vocab.def: Computers on the internet that store your files and run programs for you.
vocab.ex: Microsoft's cloud business grew very fast.

vocab.def: Money you pay every month or year to use a service.
vocab.ex: Many people now pay a subscription for Office.

vocab.def: Worth a lot of money, or very important.
vocab.ex: Microsoft became one of the most valuable companies in the world.

vocab.def: When a company decides to have fewer workers.
vocab.ex: The company cut thousands of jobs.

vocab.def: To get new knowledge or a new skill.
vocab.ex: Nadella wanted people to learn, not to know everything.

vocab_discuss: Do you use any Microsoft products? Which ones?
Is it better when people at work compete or when they share? Why?
What do you pay a subscription for? Is it worth the money?

story.heading: Part 1 — Rich, but falling behind
paras: In the 2000s, Microsoft was a very rich company.
Most computers in the world used Windows. Most offices used Office. These two products made enormous profits.
But Microsoft was losing the new markets. Google won internet search. Apple and Android won smartphones.
Microsoft made its own phones, but very few people bought them.
Inside the company, there was another problem: the culture.
Teams did not share ideas. They competed against each other.
Every year, managers had to give some workers a bad score, even when the whole team worked well. Many people said this made colleagues fight, not help each other.
The company stopped this system in 2013. In February 2014, Satya Nadella became the new boss. He was an engineer and had worked at Microsoft since 1992.
tf: In the 2000s, Microsoft made a lot of money.
Some workers got a bad score every year, even in good teams.
discuss: The company was rich but falling behind. How is this possible?
Would you like to work in a team where people compete against each other? Why or why not?

story.heading: Part 2 — A different way to think
paras: Nadella changed things quickly.
Before, Microsoft wanted everyone to use Windows. Now it put its programs on Apple and Android devices too. Office came to the iPad in 2014.
Some decisions were painful. Microsoft had bought Nokia's phone business, but it did not work. In 2015 the company lost most of that money and cut about 7,800 jobs.
Microsoft also changed how people paid. Before, you bought Office once. Now many people pay a subscription every month or year.
Nadella said the most important change was the culture. He wanted people to learn all the time, not to pretend they knew everything.
He made a mistake himself in 2014. He said something wrong about women and pay rises. On the same day, he publicly said he was wrong.
Microsoft also bought companies that people loved: the game Minecraft, LinkedIn and GitHub. It let them work in their own way.
tf: Nadella stopped Microsoft programs working on Apple devices.
The Nokia phone business was a big success.
Nadella said sorry quickly for his own mistake.
discuss: Microsoft put its programs on its rivals' phones. Why was this a clever idea?
A boss says “I was wrong” in public. Does this make people trust him more or less?

story.heading: Part 3 — Very valuable, and a new question
paras: The changes worked. Microsoft's cloud business, Azure, became one of the biggest in the world.
In 2014 the company was worth about 300 billion dollars. In 2019 it was worth one trillion. Later it was worth more than three trillion.
Then Microsoft made a big bet on artificial intelligence. It invested more than ten billion dollars in OpenAI, the company that makes ChatGPT.
It spent enormous amounts of money on new data centres. In July 2025, Microsoft was briefly worth four trillion dollars. It was one of the most valuable companies in history.
But there is a difficult part. Microsoft cut about ten thousand jobs in 2023, and thousands more in 2025. The company was making record profits at the same time.
Some people say this is normal: the company is moving money to AI. Others say the kind words about culture are easy when everything is going well.
And some experts say the cloud market helped Microsoft much more than the culture did.
So here is the question. Did the new culture change Microsoft? Or did the market change it?
tf: Microsoft was worth one trillion dollars in 2019.
Microsoft did not invest any money in artificial intelligence.
Microsoft cut jobs only when it was losing money.
discuss: Is it fair for a company to cut jobs when it is making record profits? Why or why not?
What is more important for a company's success: its culture, or the market? Say why.
Tell the story again in six sentences. Use: quickly · slowly · publicly · well · careful · difficult.

grammar.name: adjectives and adverbs
grammar.heading: Adjectives and adverbs — quick or quickly?
explain: This story is about how a company changed. To say how, we use adverbs.
Adjective — describes a noun: She is a careful driver. · The test was easy.
Adverb — describes a verb (how someone does something): She drives carefully.
Most adverbs: adjective + -ly: slow → slowly, quiet → quietly, public → publicly. If the adjective ends in -y: easy → easily, happy → happily.
Careful — irregular: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard. And hardly means almost not: I hardly slept.
After be, look, seem, feel we use an adjective: You look tired. (NOT tiredly)

practice.heading: Complete the sentences
practice.intro: Use the word in brackets as an adjective or an adverb. Change it if you need to.
items: Nadella changed many things at the company very ___. (quick)
Before an important meeting, I always read the numbers ___. (careful)
2015 was a ___ year for the people in the phone business. (difficult)
He made a mistake, and he apologised ___ on the same day. (public)
After the changes, the teams worked ___ together. (good)

fix.heading: Find the mistake
items: They work hardly every day, even at weekends.
It was a quickly change, and nobody was ready.
answers: He always drives very carefully. (how he drives = adverb)
They work hard every day, even at weekends. (hardly means almost not)
It was a quick change, and nobody was ready. (describes the noun change = adjective)

speak.label: 1 · Tell the story
paras: Tell me the Microsoft story in your own words. Six or seven sentences is enough.

speak.label: 2 · How do you do it?
paras: Tell me about something you do well, something you do slowly, and something you do carefully.
Give an example for each one.

speak.label: 3 · Teams
paras: Think of a team you have been in — at work, at school or in sport.
Did people compete or share? Was it a good team?

speak.label: 4 · Saying sorry
paras: Is it easy or difficult for you to say “I was wrong”?
Tell me about a time someone said sorry to you. How did you feel?

final: Can one new boss really change how thousands of people work? Why or why not?
Would you prefer to work for a company that is growing fast or one that is safe and slow? Why?
If you were the boss of a big company, what is the first thing you would change about the culture?
